name: Aarti Drugs Ltd
title: Aarti Drugs Ltd - 524348 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Aarti Drugs Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19% YoY to INR703.6 crore and EBITDA margin hit 13.8%, driven mainly by API price hikes.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY to INR703.6 crore and EBITDA rose 30% to INR96.9 crore, with margin up 120 bps to 13.8%. PAT fell to INR50.1 crore from INR54.0 crore, but the prior year included a INR15 crore tax refund; ex-refund PAT growth is stated at 29%. Management said API price increases tied to West Asia conflict and raw material volatility drove most growth, while volume grew about 3.5%. Sayakha utilisation rose above 60% for the first time, and the USFDA API block and Baddi formulation expansion are progressing.

vs INR54.0 crore in Q1 FY26, which included INR15 crore tax refund; ex-refund growth 29%
+20% YoY (vs INR521.3 crore); about 89% of consolidated
+149% YoY (as stated by analyst; management confirmed)

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Antibiotic 35.0%, antidiabetic 18.2%, antiprotozoal 18.5%, anti-inflammatory 11.9%, antifungal 10.2% and others 6.1% of API sales. Metformin prices are up about 20% versus pre-war levels, though below the March-April peak.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR81.6 crore, up 8% YoY, with about 74% from exports. Baddi brownfield expansion is expected to nearly double oral solid dosage capacity.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR82 crore, up 149% YoY, driven by the Sayakha plant. Methylamine ran at about 64-65% utilisation (about 60 tonnes/day, about 3,500 tonnes in the quarter).

segments.name: Salicylic acid (Tarapur)
segments.commentary: Only 67 tonnes produced in the quarter, as production was kept low. Derivatives plant (methyl salicylate, 350-400 tpm capacity) has started trials at 5-10 tonnes. Anti-dumping duty is expected in about one year.

guidance_outlook: Management says 14% EBITDA margin is achievable and 15% should be easy once the greenfield plants reach higher utilisation; a further 200 bps gain depends on prices normalising.
Volume growth of 10-15% over the next two years is seen as achievable, and about 10% even if the salicylic acid derivatives do not pick up.
Volume growth in the remaining three quarters is expected to be better than June quarter, as demand recovers once prices stabilise.
Specialty Chemicals run-rate of Q1 is expected to repeat in the next three quarters and improve further.
Captive consumption from Sayakha is expected to reach 80-90% by December quarter, adding about 1% to gross contribution at peak utilisation.
Metformin capacity to rise from 1,400 to about 2,200 tpm, including 500-550 tpm USFDA-compliant capacity taking about 10-12 months.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 greenfield assets (Sayakha, Tarapur) cost about INR600 crore and are expected to yield about 1.5x asset turn; Phase 2 brownfield projects are expected at 3-4x.
Sayakha plant utilisation was about 65% in Q1 FY27 (versus 30% in Dec-quarter and 40% in Mar-quarter, per management), with about 50% of capacity used captively for antidiabetic intermediates.
Metformin: 1,400 tpm capacity at mid-80s% utilisation; plan to scale to about 2,200 tpm, with the USFDA block (500-550 tpm) being built at Sarigam, which takes 10-12 months. US DMF already filed.

USFDA API plant (E-22): 2 main lines and 1 small line, around 4-5 active products, mostly supplied to Europe. A quasi-greenfield expansion adds 3 multipurpose lines of about 10 tpm each, more than doubling capacity.
Salicylic acid capacity about 600 tpm, utilisation about 70% per management. Derivatives plant at Tarapur (350-400 tpm) commissioned, in trial batches.
demand_pricing: Metformin pricing up about 15-20% versus pre-war; the March-April peak was higher, and prices have since eased slightly.
Price increases were tied to raw material and ammonia shortages linked to the West Asia conflict. Formulation customers cut purchases, which hit domestic volumes; export demand was less affected.
Management says Chinese competition is not a concern for its product set, though some pressure exists from select players.
Salicylic acid prices were cut sharply by Chinese players, so derivatives (salicylates) are now more profitable than salicylic acid itself.
Europe is still a small, under-tapped market for Metformin; EU CEP approvals were obtained for 9 products.

qa_highlights.question: How did metformin realizations move QoQ and YoY, and how will backward integration support market share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Harit Shah said metformin prices are up about 15-20% versus pre-war levels. Adhish Patil said the March-April peak was higher and current prices are slightly below it. Metformin capacity is about 1,400 tpm at mid-80s% utilisation, scaling to about 2,200 tpm, including 500-550 tpm USFDA capacity.

qa_highlights.question: When can API supplies to the US market start, given the USFDA block timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: US DMF is already filed. The fresh 500+ tpm block at the same location takes about 10-12 months to build, after which USFDA inspection will be sought with a customer's help. European approval exists for the same facility.

qa_highlights.question: Has the API industry entered a sustained recovery, and what is the asset turn on the INR600 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conditions remain volatile and it is too early to call. Competition from China is not an issue for its product set, though select players pressure some products. Phase 1 greenfield assets are expected to give about 1.5x asset turn; Phase 2 brownfield about 3-4x, with Sayakha about 50% of capacity used captively.

qa_highlights.question: Specialty Chemicals grew 149% to about INR82 crore: is this sustainable, and what is the methylamine run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhish Patil said the Q1 performance will repeat in the next three quarters and may improve, driven by the Sayakha plant. Methylamine ran at about 64-65% utilisation, roughly 60 tonnes per day or about 3,500 tonnes in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Tarapur salicylic acid plant and the derivatives plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Only 67 tonnes of salicylic acid were produced in the quarter as output was kept low pending equipment. The derivatives plant (350-400 tpm) has started trial batches of 5-10 tonnes. Anti-dumping duty is delayed by about a year. Chinese price cuts have made salicylates more profitable than salicylic acid.

qa_highlights.question: What were volume and price growth in Q1, and what is the outlook for the remaining three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Aggregate volume grew about 3.5% and price about 16-17% YoY, with most growth from price. Formulation buyers cut stock purchases as prices rose. Volume in the next three quarters is expected to beat the June quarter once prices stabilise, with export demand less affected.

risks_watch: Price-led growth: volume grew only about 3.5% while price rose 16-17%; management expects prices to ease as the West Asia conflict and raw-material shortages resolve, which could reduce realisations and margins.

Margin sustainability: management said 14% EBITDA margin is achievable and 15% should be easy after utilisation rises, but 200 bps further gain depends on price normalisation; Q1 also included write-offs of aged capital WIP.

Sayakha and Tarapur ramp-up: Sayakha utilisation was about 65% in Q1 against the 60-80% target; salicylic acid output of 67 tonnes and anti-dumping duty delayed by about one year keep the Tarapur drag on P&L.
US market entry timing: the USFDA-compliant metformin block (500-550 tpm) takes 10-12 months to build and then needs inspection, so US API supplies are not before about 12 months.
Formulation demand: domestic formulation customers cut purchases at high prices; management expects domestic demand recovery but cited past antibiotic and antidiarrheal demand pressure.
Q1 FY27 PAT declined to INR50.1 crore from INR54.0 crore due to the prior-year tax refund; watch whether reported PAT growth resumes in later quarters.
key_quotes: What is particularly encouraging is that despite this challenging external environment, our op erations remained completely stable throughout the quarter.
So 14% is quite doable. We are almost there.
Yes. So, this first quarter 's performance will definitely repeat for the next 3 quarters.
So achieving 10% to 15% volume growth in next two years should not be a problem.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and utilisation, with stated targets on margin and volume, but cautious on pricing, saying conditions remain volatile and it is too early to call sustained recovery. Management was evasive on the exact timing of the US API approval and on whether 200 bps of margin gain is achievable.
